name: Ezra
description: Priest living at the time of Exile and Return

points: Ezra went up from Babylon a ready scribe in the law of Moses, and the king granted all his requests because the hand of the Most High was upon him.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

points: Ezra had prepared his heart, his mind, to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments. We are in captivity, working and tired, and the Most High reminds us these are the last days, so prepare your mind.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

points: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself, and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

points: Artaxerxes' letter names Ezra a scribe of the law of the God of heaven and grants that any of Israel who willingly desire may go up to Jerusalem with him.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

points: Artaxerxes decreed to the treasurers beyond the river to supply Ezra speedily with silver, wheat, wine, oil, and salt, so that no wrath would come against the king and his sons.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

points: Ezra was told, after the wisdom of his God in his hand, to set magistrates and judges to judge the people and to teach those who did not know the laws of the Most High.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

points: When Ezra had prayed and confessed, weeping and casting himself down before the house of God, a very great congregation of men, women, and children assembles to him, for the people wept very sore.

note.label: Ezra 10: The Covenant to Put Away Strange Wives

points: Then Ezra rises and makes the chief priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do according to this word, and they swear, the same way an oath was made to keep the commandments.

note.label: Ezra 10: The Covenant to Put Away Strange Wives

points: Ezra rises from before the house of God and goes into the chamber of Johanan, and eats no bread nor drinks water, for he mourns because of the transgression of them that had been carried away.

note.label: Ezra 10: The Covenant to Put Away Strange Wives

points: Ezra the priest stands and says they have transgressed and taken strange wives to increase the trespass of Israel.

note.label: Ezra 10: The Covenant to Put Away Strange Wives

points: The children of the captivity do so; Ezra and certain chief of the fathers, separated by name, sit down on the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.

note.label: Ezra 10: The Covenant to Put Away Strange Wives

points: Ezra stands upon a pulpit of wood with brothers on his right hand and brothers on his left hand, and opens the book in the sight of all the people, blessing the Most High, to whom the people answer, Amen, Amen.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

points: Nehemiah, Ezra, and the Levites tell the people the day is holy and they should not mourn or weep, for the people wept when they heard the words of the law.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

points: On the second day the chief of the fathers, the priests, and the Levites gather to Ezra to understand the words of the law, and they find written that Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

points: The companies are named, priests with trumpets and Levites with the musical instruments of David the man of God, Ezra the scribe going before one and Nehemiah with the other, until the two companies stood in the house of God.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall
